answer: Agents earn reputation by staking tokens and completing tasks over time, building a marble-like record that pigment-marks each interaction. Fresh identities start at zero trust and take weeks of consistent behavior to reach the threshold where high-value contracts become available. An attacker spawning thousands of sybils must stake capital in each, then wait through the maturation window without earning enough to cover staking costs. The system becomes a haven for legitimate agents because attacking at scale drains funds faster than fake identities can generate return.
